links.outcome: Proportion of hematologists reporting a written institutional AI policy
links.effect: Only 4.8% reported a written institutional AI policy, while 87% reported clinical AI use in the prior three months.
links.quote: whereas only 4.8% reported a written institutional AI policy

links.outcome: Entry of patient data into non-approved public chatbots
links.effect: 48.6% had entered patient data into non-approved public chatbots (8.2% identifiable).
links.quote: Nearly half (48.6%) had entered patient data into non-approved public chatbots (8.2% identifiable), whereas only 4.8% reported a written institutional AI policy.

links.outcome: Staff entering patient data into unapproved public generative AI tools
links.effect: 48.6% entered patient data into non-approved public chatbots; 8.2% entered identifiable data.
links.quote: Nearly half (48.6%) had entered patient data into non-approved public chatbots (8.2% identifiable), whereas only 4.8% reported a written institutional AI policy.

links.outcome: Receipt of structured AI training among clinical AI users
links.effect: 87% reported clinical AI use in prior three months, yet only 14% had received structured AI training.
links.quote: Clinical AI use in the prior three months was reported by 87%, yet only 14% had received structured AI training.

links.outcome: Encountering fabricated references or incorrect information from generative AI in research/writing
links.effect: 55.5% used generative AI for research/writing; 81% of them had encountered fabricated references or incorrect information.
links.quote: Generative AI for research/writing was used by 55.5%, of whom 81% had encountered fabricated references or incorrect information.

screen.reason: National survey of hematologists assessing real-world use, knowledge, attitudes, and governance/safety practices (e.g., patient data privacy risks) regarding AI/LLMs in clinical practice and research.
